land.text: British Guiana: 'In 1831, the united colonies of Demerara-Essequibo and separate colony of Berbice together became a single British colony'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire shapes 1958-1962 and 1963-1968 still list Guyana among their modern countries and the 1967 BCE shape covers all 830 cells of Guyana's own shape, so the BCE row keeps the colony two years after independence (26 May 1966); the British Colonial Empire dossier should release it in 1966.

capitals.name: Georgetown
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Georgetown'; the page gives no earlier capital of British Guiana, so the 1966 start is the state's.

correction.text: the 1967 shape unchanged, carried back to independence: 'Guyana achieved independence from the United Kingdom as a dominion on 26 May 1966'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Guyana shape begins in 1967 but the page dates independence to 26 May 1966, so the same shape is used for 1966.

212,448 km2 against the infobox 214,969 km2 (ratio 0.99). The shape equals modern Guyana (830 cells against 825 for Natural Earth's Guyana, with no cell shared with the Venezuela, Suriname or Brazil shapes): it therefore draws as Guyanese both the land west of the Essequibo that Venezuela claims and the New River Triangle that Suriname claims, which is right because Guyana held both (Venezuela holds only Ankoko island, below the grid's cell size). Brazil in the seed's modern_countries is an edge artefact.
Same polygon as 1967-2023; the page still gives 214,969 km2. The March 2024 Venezuelan law making Essequibo a Venezuelan state (Guayana Esequiba page) changes nothing on the ground.

region.text: British Guiana, the colony formed in 1831 from Demerara-Essequibo and Berbice, independent as Guyana

ledger.note: 26 May 1966: British Guiana becomes independent Guyana. 'Guyana achieved independence from the United Kingdom as a dominion on 26 May 1966'; infobox 'Independence from the United Kingdom as Guyana: 26 May 1966'. The page does not trace the 1966 frontier; the land is the modern country, including the Essequibo west of the river (claimed by Venezuela) and the New River Triangle (claimed by Suriname).

region.text: Ankoko island and surrounding islands at the confluence of the Cuyuni and Wenamu rivers (6.717 N, 61.133 W on the Ankoko Island page)

ledger.note: October 1966: Venezuelan troops occupy Ankoko Island, five months after independence. 'Venezuelan troops began their occupation of Ankoko Island in October 1966'; the Guayana Esequiba page adds that Venezuela rejected Guyana's protest and kept the island under Venezuelan administration. The island is far below the 253 km2 grid cell, so the region is a 15 km circle clipped to Guyana.

region.text: the New River Triangle, 'a forested area in the East Berbice-Corentyne region of Guyana' between the New River and the Corentyne (header coordinate 2.5 N, 57.25 W)

ledger.note: 12 December 1967: Guyanese police land at Oronoque in the New River Triangle, which Suriname had occupied with posts. 'On 12 December 1967, four armed men of the Guyana police force landed at Oronoque'; of Suriname's four military posts 'only Camp Tigri (also known as Camp Jaguar) remained'. The page does not date the posts, so this is the first dated action on the ground; the region is the page's coordinate with a radius (the page gives no area). Counterpart dutch-suriname: in 1967-1969 Suriname 'was still a constituent state of the Kingdom of the Netherlands' (New River Triangle page) and the posts were 'established by the Surinamese army'; republic-of-suriname begins only in 1975.

region.text: the New River Triangle, 'a forested area in the East Berbice-Corentyne region of Guyana' between the New River and the Corentyne (header coordinate 2.5 N, 57.25 W)

ledger.note: 1969: the Guyana Defence Force takes full control of the New River Triangle. 'In 1969, three years after its independence, the Guyana Defence Force (GDF) seized full control'; border skirmishes at Camp Tigri on 19 August 1969. In November 1970 both governments agreed in Trinidad and Tobago to withdraw, but 'Guyana has not held upon this agreement and continue to occupy the New River Triangle'. Suriname's claim survives and passes to republic-of-suriname in 1975; the counterpart here is dutch-suriname, the dossier of Suriname before independence.
23 February 1970: Guyana becomes a republic. The page says Guyana 'became a republic on 23 February 1970' (infobox 'Republic: 23 February 1970'); same state, no change of land.

region.text: Ankoko island and surrounding islands at the confluence of the Cuyuni and Wenamu rivers (6.717 N, 61.133 W on the Ankoko Island page)

ledger.note: Still in force when the record ends: 'The island remains under Venezuelan administration, where a Venezuelan airport and a military base operate.' This event only closes the 1966 occupation_start at the last year of the record; the Guayana Esequiba page says the territory 'excluding the Venezuelan-controlled Ankoko Island, is controlled by Guyana'.

wars.name: Ankoko occupation and Rupununi uprising (Essequibo dispute)

zones.text: Ankoko island and surrounding islands at the confluence of the Cuyuni and Wenamu rivers (6.717 N, 61.133 W on the Ankoko Island page)

wars.outcome: Venezuela kept Ankoko Island; Guyana kept the rest of the land west of the Essequibo. The 1970 Protocol of Port of Spain 'declared a 12-year moratorium on Venezuela's reclamation of the Essequibo'.
wars.note: Geneva Agreement signed 17 February 1966; Venezuelan occupation of Ankoko in October 1966; on 2 January 1969 rebels 'began their attacks on Lethem' and Guyana accused Venezuela of helping them (Venezuela rejected this). The page does not say the rebels held ground. The 159,500 km2 'area west of the Essequibo River' is only claimed, never held by Venezuela, so it is not a contest zone; the moratorium was not renewed in 1983.

wars.name: Tigri Area (New River Triangle) clashes with Suriname

zones.text: the New River Triangle, 'a forested area in the East Berbice-Corentyne region of Guyana' between the New River and the Corentyne (header coordinate 2.5 N, 57.25 W)

wars.outcome: Guyana seized full control in 1969; the November 1970 agreement to withdraw was not kept and Guyana still holds the Triangle, which Suriname claims.
wars.note: The Surinamese side was a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands until 25 November 1975; the page speaks of 'Surinamese militias'. Pre-history: the 1814 treaty set the Courantyne as the border, Schomburgk surveyed it in 1840 and Brown found the New River in 1871.

wars.name: Essequibo crisis of 2023-2024
wars.outcome: No change on the ground: Venezuela held a referendum in December 2023 ('No vote was held in the disputed region') and in March 2024 passed a law designating Essequibo as a new Venezuelan state.
wars.note: ICJ: Guterres concluded the Good Offices Process had failed in January 2018; on 18 December 2020 the court 'ruled that it had jurisdiction and accepted the case'.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow the 1814 treaty line on the Courantyne and the 1899 Paris award (Schomburgk Line with two deviations) on the Venezuelan side; two stretches are disputed but held by Guyana: the land west of the Essequibo (Venezuela's claim) and the New River Triangle (Suriname's claim), and Ankoko Island is Venezuelan-held.

notes: Guyana (4 pages opened against a budget of 1-2: the two territorial events each needed a page for their date and coordinates). Cliopatria's 1967 and 2024 polygons are modern Guyana; independence was 26 May 1966, so a 1966 keyframe is added. The British Colonial Empire row (eu-11) still covers Guyana until 1968. Venezuela's claim (159,500 km2 west of the Essequibo) and Suriname's claim (New River Triangle) are drawn inside Guyana, as held; only Ankoko Island is Venezuelan-held and is far below the grid cell. The ongoing Ankoko occupation has an occupation_end at 2024 only to close the pair (confidence 1). Gazetteer: the admin1 name 'East Berbice-Corentyne' resolves to cells near Georgetown (-58.26, 6.29..6.76), not to the New River Triangle, so a radius around the page's coordinate is used instead; names the gazetteer lacks: Ankoko Island (place, 6.717 N 61.133 W), New River Triangle / Tigri Area (region, 2.5 N 57.25 W), Guayana Esequiba (region, Guyana west of the Essequibo, about 159,500 km2 on the page; here approximated by no polygon). The Rupununi uprising of January 1969 is not given a held territory by the page, so no rebel dossier is written.
